curriculum.lesson_evidence: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have diverse stories, languages and knowledge systems. Study First Nations stories and voices only through classroom-approved published texts or materials guided by Aboriginal educators. Name Country or community only when the source does. Do not invent Dreaming stories, sacred meanings or ceremonial content.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
List three respectful research actions and one action to avoid when reading First Nations texts.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Use approved sources; credit creators; do not invent sacred content. Avoid: copying restricted stories as dress-ups.

CHECK
Treating First Nations cultures as one single story. Diversity and protocols matter.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Using only teacher-approved texts, complete a source card (creator, source title, named Country/community if given, theme in the creator's terms) and two questions for Community educators.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

Study First Nations stories and voices only through classroom-approved published texts or materials guided by Aboriginal educators. Name Country or community only when the source does. WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.
